title: install_e2e's setup_file swallows a refused commit, so it surfaces later as a misleading dirty-tree refusal
body:
## Summary

`opt/utilz/test/install_e2e.bats`'s `setup_file` copies the checkout, stages everything, and commits inside the copy so the publish's dirty-tree gate is satisfied:

```
git -C "$src" add -A >/dev/null 2>&1
git -C "$src" -c user.email=e2e@example.com -c user.name=e2e \
  commit -qm "e2e fixture" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
```

(`install_e2e.bats:40-42`). **The project's pre-commit hooks run inside the copy. When one refuses, `|| true` swallows the refusal, the copy stays dirty, and the failure surfaces a step later as the publish's correct "source tree is dirty" refusal**, which names the wrong cause and points nowhere near the gate that actually said no.

## How it was found

2026-09-14, during cc's gate run for issue 0024: `utilz test utilz` failed with `not ok 120 setup_file failed ... source tree is dirty`. The real cause was the pre-commit doctor gate refusing every commit: the view skew on issues 0025 to 0027 that vc fixed at `895a2fc`. The setup's own output said "dirty tree". cc found the mechanism by reproducing the copy-commit in a scratch rsync of the tree with its output visible. vc named the `|| true` as a swallowed error and routed it to cc, as finder and fixer.

## Why the `|| true` is there

When the real checkout is clean, `git add -A` stages nothing and `git commit` exits 1 with "nothing to commit"; the `|| true` absorbs exactly that. **It cannot tell that case from a commit a hook refused**, and the second case is the one that matters.

## Fix direction

Tell the two cases apart instead of discarding both:

- After `git add -A`, commit only when the index differs from HEAD (`git diff --cached --quiet` returns non-zero).
- If that commit then fails, fail `setup_file` loudly, name the refused commit, and print its output.

This is IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001. The proof is a copy whose commit a hook refuses, which must fail naming the commit, not the dirty tree. How that is shown, and why it is not a new test, is in the widened scope below.

## Scope, widened on hv's word

The stage-and-commit pair is not install_e2e's alone. Six test files carry their own copy of it, each discarding git's output, so a refusal anywhere fails with no reason given, and install_e2e's copy alone also swallows it:

- `install_e2e.bats:40-42`
- `install.bats:26-27`
- `install_lib.bats:239-240`
- `relink.bats:193-194`
- `upgrade.bats:30-31`
- `test_helper.bash:461-462`

Three more fixture helpers are repeated across the same files, each copy identical in behaviour: `run_install_function` in five (install, install_lib, install_guards, relink, upgrade), `run_publish` in two (install, upgrade) and `set_prefix_key` in two (install, relink). hv, 2026-09-14: "Fix it! That is a clear highlander violation."

One home for all of them, in `test_helper.bash` beside `make_fake_src`:

- `fixture_commit <tree> <message>` stages everything and commits only when the index differs from HEAD. It fails naming the tree, the commit and git's own output when the staging, the comparison or the commit fails, and when the tree is still dirty afterwards.
- `run_install_function`, `run_publish` and `set_prefix_key` move there unchanged, and every local copy goes.
- `gitz.bats:25` is left alone: it builds a repo for gitz to inspect, stages one named file, and keeps git's output. It is a different fixture, not a copy of this one.

**The proof is a one-off demonstration, not a new test.** A permanent test whose subject is a test helper is a test of a test, which hv's standing direction (2026-09-11) rules out. A fixture whose commit a hook refuses is driven once through HEAD's logic and once through `fixture_commit`, and both outputs go in the commit. The suites that use the helpers are the regression guard.

## Severity

Low. Test-harness only, and the failure was already loud; it was misattributed, which cost a diagnosis rather than a defect.

Filed by cc on 2026-09-14. The fix lands after vc's verdict on 0024 and before 0016, as its own commit.

## Resolution, 2026-09-14

Fixed by cc, the finder, at `9cb548c`, on hv's word widening it, which hv confirmed to vc directly the same day. `test_helper.bash`'s ST0014 INSTALL FIXTURES section is now the one home for `fixture_commit`, `run_install_function`, `run_publish` and `set_prefix_key`, and every local copy is gone: six stage-and-commit pairs, five `run_install_function`, two `run_publish` and two `set_prefix_key`. `install_e2e`'s `setup_file` now runs `fixture_commit "$src" "e2e fixture" || return 1`. `fixture_commit` commits only when the index differs from HEAD, and fails by name, with git's own output, when the staging, the comparison or the commit fails, or when the tree is still dirty afterwards.

Verified by vc, the reviewer. The moved helpers carry the removed copies' bodies unchanged; the stage-and-commit copies differed only in `install_e2e`'s identity, `e2e@example.com`, which nothing reads. No definition of the four fixtures and no `git add -A` remain outside `test_helper.bash`, and `gitz.bats:25` builds a different repo and is rightly left alone. cc's demonstration, replayed by vc at `b14bbc0`, gave cc's results case for case: HEAD's logic exits 0 with the hook's refusal swallowed and the tree left dirty, while `fixture_commit` exits 1 naming the refused commit; a hook that dirties the tree is named; a tree already at HEAD commits nothing; an unborn branch gets its first commit. `utilz test utilz` under /bin/bash 3.2.57 at `a89e21a`: 219 of 219, with the two skips the environment's own, and each of the six fixture suites keeps the test count it had before. Closed by vc, the reviewer, not the fixer.
